decision.title: Source locations for parsed input documents (packet )

item.p: Header (additive after , packet ): include/sxml/processor.h gains sxml_source_location_policy (AUTOMATIC = 0, ALWAYS, NEVER) and, at the end of sxml_processor_configuration, sxml_source_location_policy source_location_policy; (another value makes the configuration invalid). include/sxml/tree.h (frozen) gains one function, sxml_node_get_location(node, &location): dm:location over the tree's get_location, line 0 when unknown, for hosts (the CLI's error report, which uses the public API only) and for sxml's own copies. Nothing else in a frozen header changes.

The program's flag (glossary ): one bool per IR unit, set by sxml_ir_unit_add_expression and _replace_expression when a STATIC_CALL or FUNCTION_REFERENCE names a native row with the new property SXML_NATIVE_FUNCTION_READS_SOURCE_LOCATIONS: fn:location, fn:function-lookup, fn:load-xquery-module, fn:transform and xsl:evaluate's row. One place for XPath, XQuery and XSLT, no pass and no new IR kind. sxml_ir_unit_set_reads_source_locations is for a front end whose reports need locations (Schematron, 7.28: 's node_location). A unit whose in-scope schemas include any but the processor's built-in ones also reads them (it can validate, sxml_processor_unit_reads_source_locations).

What AUTOMATIC decides by (glossary , in the processor): whether a program has been compiled, whether one of those reads locations (noted by the public compile functions of XPath, XQuery and XSLT, and by sxml_schema_initialize: a schema is a validation; the processor's built-in schemas leave it as it was), and the evaluation in progress. sxml_evaluate_unit begins and ends each evaluation with its unit's answer, or'ed with the enclosing evaluation's (fn:transform, fn:load-xquery-module, a host function). sxml_processor_parse_document, the one parse behind fn:doc, fn:document, fn:parse-xml, the CLI's fn:collection and a resolver's DOCUMENT_NODE, keeps locations when: ALWAYS; never under NEVER; under AUTOMATIC, during an evaluation as it says, otherwise when no program has been compiled or one compiled reads them (, 7).

Copies keep what they copy: sxml_tree_builder_copy_node passes each node's location in its events when the copied root has one (one question per copy, so a copy of a tree without locations costs nothing more), and XSLT's whitespace-stripped source documents (src/xslt_whitespace.c) keep locations when the document did; so location(.) answers for a stylesheet's input under xsl:strip-space, and a validated copy keeps its input's lines.

Errors (, 8): an error "names an input node" when its value ($err:value: fn:error's third argument, an xsl:message's select) holds a node; the record's own location stays the expression's (the frozen sxml_error_record has one), and the CLI prints a second line FILE:LINE:COLUMN: the node the error names for the first node of the value whose document kept locations (sxml_query_run_fail). src/evaluator.c is unchanged. fn:error is not a reason to keep locations ('s list is the owner's); --locations=always gives them to a program that cannot ask.

CLI: --locations=automatic|always|never for xpath, xquery and transform (SXML_QUERY_LOCATIONS_OPTION); xpath and xquery compile before they parse --context-item (sxml_query_run_read_context_item), so a static error is now reported before a context document that does not parse. 9 CLI tests, 21 goldens with the new usage line.

Measured (release, the 26 MB, 2.5 million node document of , peak RSS): xpath --context-item count(//line) 173 MB under automatic and never, 249 MB under always; location((//line)[last()]) 249 MB under automatic; xquery count(doc(...)//line) 175 MB automatic, 251 MB always; transform with count(//line) 174 MB automatic, 250 MB with location(). Before the change every case was 171-175 MB.
